sourceObjectiveEnglish: Explain what needs doing: Necesitar + infinitive expresses a need.
sourceSpeakingEnglish: Role-play Preparar un examen with a patient classmate. Practice explain what needs doing. Use this lesson's grammar, ask a related question, answer the partner, and confirm understanding. Keep language at beginner level; explain unfamiliar words in English when asked.

sourceGrammarEnglish.focus: Necesitar + infinitive expresses a need. Tener que + infinitive expresses an obligation: necesito estudiar; tengo que estudiar. Keep que after tener.

examples.es: Tenemos que estudiar para el examen.
examples.en: We have to study for the exam.
I need to review the questions.

cards.decisionNote: Spanish el marks masculine singular; French le has elision and contextual article behavior.
Source la groups feminine article, object it and her; no one French isolated face preserves all roles.
Source en groups in/on/at; French choice depends on location, time and phrase.
Source tengo is stand-alone I have; French j’ai needs a subject and clitic agreement context.
Source necesito is stand-alone I need; French avoir besoin de needs a complement, while devoir can signal obligation.
Spanish los is masculine plural article/object; French les loses the source gender marking.
Spanish las is feminine plural article/object; French les loses the source gender marking.
Source para groups for and in order to; French pour needs a phrase-level object or infinitive context.

cards.sourceSpanish: Tenemos que estudiar para el examen.
cards.sourceEnglish: We have to study for the exam.
I need to review the questions.
cards.proposedFrench: J’ai besoin de réviser les questions.
cards.decisionNote: Need in the source is distinct from obligation; review avoir besoin de plus infinitive in this classroom idiom.

cards.sourceSpanish: Julia tiene que terminar dos páginas.
cards.sourceEnglish: Julia has to finish two pages.

cards.proposedFrench: Diego a besoin de son livre.
cards.decisionNote: Spanish su may be his or her; Diego's ownership supports son livre in this scene, subject to source review.

cards.sourceEnglish: We can practice together at home.
cards.proposedFrench: Nous pouvons nous entraîner ensemble à la maison.
cards.decisionNote: Practice together is conditional as nous entraîner ensemble; a general pratiquer translation may shift the classroom sense.

cards.sourceSpanish: No tenemos que aprender todo hoy.
cards.sourceEnglish: We do not have to learn everything today.
cards.proposedFrench: Nous n’avons pas besoin de tout apprendre aujourd’hui.
cards.decisionNote: No tenemos que expresses lack of obligation, not prohibition. French n’avons pas besoin de keeps that distinction.

cards.sourceEnglish: I need to review the verbs.
cards.proposedFrench: J’ai besoin de réviser les verbes.

cards.sourceEnglish: I have to finish the homework.
cards.decisionNote: Source la tarea is the homework; French les devoirs plural changes noun number convention, not task count.

reader.sourceSpanish: Tenemos que llegar a las ocho.
reader.sourceEnglish: We have to arrive at eight.
reader.proposedFrench: Nous devons arriver à huit heures.
reader.decisionNote: Llegar a las ocho means arrive at eight, not study at eight.

reader.decisionNote: Spanish necesitas is informal singular; tu is conditional on the source speaking relationship.

archivedRedesign.title: Transformer une demande en tâches prioritaires
archivedRedesign.scene: Une coordinatrice prépare une petite exposition. L’équipe doit séparer les tâches obligatoires des améliorations facultatives et définir qui valide le résultat.
archivedRedesign.reason: The archived small-exhibition coordinator task changes the source exam-preparation scene and objective.

sourceDecisions: The Spanish source contrasts necesitar + infinitive (need) with tener que + infinitive (obligation). French avoir besoin de and devoir need distinct authored grammar and non-obligation examples.
The source places a beginner need/obligation lesson at Master 13; curriculum placement needs review without changing saved lesson identity.
Grouped articles, object pronouns, en, para and gendered Spanish plurals require contextual French dictionary and scoring senses.
The source's informal necesitas and possessive su require person/register/context decisions before French answers are selected.
